content: Letter to Ibn Turka in MS Majlis 10196 (front matter), from Sayyid Ḥusayn Akhlāṭī: a warm letter urging his accomplished disciple, whom he calls khalīlī (my bosom companion) and the leading luminary among his circle of brethren, to write a work establishing the propositions and conjunctions proper to the science of letters (MK: perhaps the Mafāḥiṣ?). It closes with a brief lettrist analysis of a hadith on food, seemingly alluding to a recent stay by Ibn Turka at Akhlāṭī's residence (edition in P.2.2). MK's footnote cites Gāzurgāhī that Akhlāṭī's disciples, including Ibn Turka, Yazdī and Qāżīzāda Rūmī, did spiritual exercises in a room under his house.
